newsitem.title: INDIA: India, Russia near nuclear power plant deal.
newsitem.headline: India, Russia near nuclear power plant deal.

text.p: Russia and India are nearing agreement on the construction of a 2,000-megawatt nuclear power project in southern India which was first proposed in 1988, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Davydov said on Monday.
Davydov told a news conference in the Indian capital that the nuclear plant would be built in Kudankulam town in Tamil Nadu state.
"We are quite near to concluding final agreement with India about this project. This is in two blocks, one million kilowatts each, and the type is lightwater reactor," Davydov said.
The project was first proposed in 1988 during a visit to India by former Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev.
A Russian official who asked not to be identified said the project languished following the breakup of the Soviet Union.
Davydov said he did not have the exact cost of the project but Russia would offer credit to India to pay for it.

Davydov was on a five-day visit to India to promote trade between the two countries. He was scheduled to meet Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram.
He said the two countries needed to improve their infrastructure, including banking services, if trade was to be increased.

"We need to improve the infrastructure for trade. There is not even a single Russian bank operating in India or an Indian bank in Russia. We are dealing through third countries," said Davydov, who is also minister of foreign trade.
Davydov said there was the potential for increased Indian sales to Russia as his country already imports $50 billion worth of goods every year.

Between 1990/91 (April-March) and 1992/93, India's trade with the former Soviet republics fell almost 90 percent as the breakup of the Soviet Union disrupted commercial ties, according to official Indian estimates.

In 1995/96, bilateral trade between India and the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) stood at 77.08 billion rupees ($2.16 billion). Russia accounted for about 70 percent of the imports of CIS member states, and 92 percent of exports to India, officials said.
Davydov's visit to the Indian capital came a week after that of Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov.
During Rodionov's visit, New Delhi and Moscow discussed but failed to sign an agreement, reported to be worth $1.8 billion, on the sale of 40 multi-purpose Sukhoi Su-30 warplanes.
Davydov said Russia would be willing to offer India credit if it decided to buy the jets. "If you are ready to buy, we will give you the credit," he said.
As the its main non-communist ally, India was one of Moscow's biggest arms clients before the breakup of the Soviet Union.
